Project Treble is a major re-architect of the Android OS framework introduced by Google in May 2017 with the announcement of Android 8.0 [1]. It was designed to make it easier, faster, and less costly for manufacturers to update devices to newer versions of Android, and to streamline the development and deployment of updates via Google Play Services while reducing manufacturers' involvement in the update [1][2].

Project Treble achieves this by separating the device-specific, lower-level vendor implementation from the Android OS framework using a new stable "vendor interface" [1]. This interface provides access to the hardware-specific parts of Android, allowing device makers to deliver new Android releases by simply updating the OS framework without requiring additional work from silicon manufacturers [1].

Semantic search is search with meaning that seeks to improve accuracy by understanding the searcher's intent and contextual meaning of terms [1]. Modern systems use vector embeddings to convert words, phrases, or documents into numerical vectors, allowing the engine to find results based on meaning rather than exact keyword matches [1].

In contrast, lexical search involves the search engine looking for literal matches of the query words or variants of them without understanding the overall meaning of the query [1].

Deepfakes are images, videos, or audio that have been edited or generated using artificial intelligence, AI-based tools, or audio-video editing software [1]. The term is a portmanteau of "deep learning" and "fake" [1]. 

They can depict real or fictional people and are considered a form of synthetic media created by combining various media elements into a new artifact [1].

Algorithmic bias describes a systematic and repeatable harmful tendency in computerized sociotechnical systems to create unfair outcomes, such as privileging one category or arbitrary group over another [1][2]. This can happen in ways that differ from or align with the intended function of the algorithm, and it can be either intentional or unintentional [1][2].

The study of algorithmic bias focuses primarily on algorithms that reflect systematic and unfair discrimination [1]. It can emerge from factors such as biased design decisions, pre-existing expectations, feature and label choices, or the way data is coded, collected, selected, and used for training [1][3].
In March 2016, AlphaGo beat the South Korean professional Go player Lee Sedol in a five-game match [1][2].

Prompt engineering is the process of structuring natural language inputs, known as prompts, to produce specified outputs from a generative AI model [1]. It can also be defined as the practice of designing and refining input instructions given to an AI model to achieve more accurate, relevant, or useful outputs [1][2]. 

The Oxford English Dictionary defines it as the discipline or profession concerned with formulating and refining prompts for an AI program or algorithm to optimize its output or achieve a desired outcome [2].

An AI hallucination is a response generated by an artificial intelligence that presents false or misleading information as fact [1]. These responses can include plausible-sounding random falsehoods, such as invented citations or lyrics [1][3]. 

The term is also used in computer vision to describe adding detail to an image to improve it, such as generating high-resolution faces from low-resolution inputs [2].
